mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: Medhas, the seer, resumes his account to King Suratha: with this mantra the Uttama Carita, the third and longest story (chapters 5–13), begins. In the Gita Press pāṭha the mantra carries the bīja ॐ क्लीं, which belongs to the recitation, not to the Purāṇa, and the carita is preceded by its own viniyoga and dhyāna.

sandhi.note: Final m stands before the vowel of असुराभ्याम् and is written with it. The m of असुराभ्याम् becomes anusvāra before the ś of शचीपतेः (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).
Visarga before c becomes s, and s next to c becomes ś.
-āḥ before a voiced sound: the visarga (as ru) becomes y, and before a consonant that y is always lost, leaving -ā.

samasa.sense: the two asura brothers who rule the third story; the dual ending covers both
of Indra, king of the gods
the offerings that belong to the gods
samasa.alt: Also यज्ञे भागाः (saptamī tatpuruṣa), ‘shares in the sacrifice’; the sense is the same.

samasa.vigraha: मदबलस्य आश्रयः, तस्मात् (मदः च बलं च = मदबलम्)
samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, its first member a dvandva
samasa.literal: from resort to pride and strength
samasa.sense: because they trusted in their arrogance and their might
samasa.alt: मदबल can also be read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, मदस्य बलम्, ‘the strength of arrogance’; the dvandva gives the more natural pair.

morph.note: Past passive participle of √हृ used as a finite verb (‘were seized’). With subjects of different gender and number (त्रैलोक्यम् n. sg., यज्ञभागाः m. pl.) it agrees with the nearer one.
Taddhita with vṛddhi of the first syllable: त्रिलोक → त्रैलोक्य, ‘the three worlds’ taken as one whole, i.e. sovereignty over them.

mantras.anvaya: पुरा मदबलाश्रयात् शुम्भनिशुम्भाभ्याम् असुराभ्याम् शचीपतेः त्रैलोक्यम् यज्ञभागाः च हृताः।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive sentence: the agents in the instrumental (शुम्भनिशुम्भाभ्याम् असुराभ्याम्), the things seized in the nominative (त्रैलोक्यम् यज्ञभागाः च), the cause in the ablative (मदबलाश्रयात्).
mantras.lit: Formerly, by the two asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha, through reliance on (their) pride and strength, the three worlds and the sacrificial shares of Śacī’s lord were taken away.
mantras.tr: Long ago the asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha, trusting in their pride and their strength, seized from Indra, Śacī’s lord, the three worlds and his share of the sacrifices.
mantras.tr_note: The passive is turned into an active sentence; ‘from Indra’ renders the genitive शचीपतेः.

comm.t: Medhas opens the third story with a usurpation, as he opened the second (2.2–3): the demons take Indra’s rule over the three worlds and the gods’ shares of the sacrifice. This time the enemies are two brothers, Śumbha and Niśumbha, and their strength is said to rest on pride (मद).

In the Gita Press pāṭha the Uttama Carita has its own viniyoga: Rudra is its ṛṣi, Mahāsarasvatī its devatā, anuṣṭubh its metre; its dhyāna pictures Mahāsarasvatī as born from the body of Gaurī and as the destroyer of Śumbha and the other daityas. This assignment is liturgical tradition, not part of the Purāṇa’s narrative.

Final t becomes d before a vowel.

sandhi.note: Final m is written together with the following vowel; before य of याम्यम् and च the m becomes anusvāra.

morph.note: Perfect of √कृ, third person dual, ātmanepada: च-क्र-आते. √कृ is ubhayapadī; the next verse uses the parasmaipada dual चक्रतुः for the same subject. The ātmanepada suits the sense ‘made (it) their own’.
The abstract suffix -tā (tal) makes a feminine noun of state from सूर्य: ‘Sun-ness’, i.e. the Sun’s function.
Taddhita with vṛddhi of the first vowel (इ → ऐ) and guṇa of the final u (u → av): इन्दु → ऐन्दव ‘belonging to the Moon’. कौबेर and याम्य are formed the same way from कुबेर and यम.

mantras.anvaya: तौ एव सूर्यताम्, तद्वत् ऐन्दवम् अधिकारम्, तथा कौबेरम् अथ याम्यम् वरुणस्य च (अधिकारम्) चक्राते।
mantras.anvaya_en: One verb (चक्राते) with a list of objects: the Sun’s state, and the offices of the Moon, Kubera, Yama and Varuṇa; अधिकारम् is understood with each adjective, and वरुणस्य is a genitive standing for a fifth.
mantras.lit: Those two themselves took over the state of the Sun, likewise the office of the Moon, so too that of Kubera, and of Yama, and of Varuṇa.
mantras.tr: They seized for themselves the Sun’s place, and in the same way the offices of the Moon, of Kubera, of Yama and of Varuṇa.

comm.t: The brothers do not merely defeat the gods; they take over their functions in the cosmos one by one: the Sun, the Moon, Kubera (wealth), Yama (death) and Varuṇa (the waters).

The list repeats the complaint of the gods against Mahiṣa in 2.6 (सूर्येन्द्राग्न्यनिलेन्दूनां यमस्य वरुणस्य च … अधिकारान्). Each carita begins with the order of the worlds overturned; the Goddess appears to restore it.

samasa.literal: those whose kingdom has fallen away
samasa.sense: the gods, stripped of their rule

morph.note: Perfect of √कृ, third person dual, parasmaipada (च-क्र-अतुः). The previous verse used the ātmanepada चक्राते for the same two subjects; both voices of this ubhayapadī root are used side by side.
भ्रष्ट is the past participle of √भ्रंश् ‘to fall’: the nasal is lost and ś + t gives ṣṭ.
Past participle of √धू with two prefixes, वि and निर्: ‘shaken off completely’, i.e. expelled. The participles serve as predicates; the verb ‘were’ is understood.

mantras.anvaya: तौ एव पवनर्द्धिम् च वह्निकर्म च चक्रतुः। ततः देवाः पराजिताः भ्रष्टराज्याः विनिर्धूताः (अभवन्)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line completes the list of 5.3 with a new verb; the second is a nominal sentence of three participles with देवाः as subject.
mantras.lit: Those two themselves took over the might of the Wind and the work of Fire. Then the gods, defeated, their kingdom lost, were driven out.
mantras.tr: They took the Wind’s power too, and the office of Fire. So the gods, defeated and stripped of their kingdom, were cast out.

comm.t: The usurpation is complete: Wind and Fire follow Sun, Moon, Kubera, Yama and Varuṇa. The second line gives the result in three participles: defeated, kingdomless, expelled.
Fire (वह्नि) carries the offerings to the gods; its work in demon hands means the sacrifice itself no longer reaches them, which completes the loss of the यज्ञभागाः named in 5.2.

samasa.literal: those whose office has been taken
samasa.sense: the gods, robbed of their cosmic functions (5.3–4)

samasa.literal: those whose count is ten thrice
samasa.sense: the gods, ‘the Thirty’ (a round number for the thirty-three)
samasa.alt: Also explained from दशा ‘stage of life’ (the gods who remain always in the third stage, youth); the numerical sense is the usual one.

samasa.vigraha: महान्तौ च तौ असुरौ च, ताभ्याम्

samasa.sense: the Unconquered: her epithet, set against the defeated gods (पराजिताः, 5.4)

morph.note: Present of सम् + √स्मृ (guṇa स्मर-), used as a historic present in narrative: ‘they remembered’.
Past participle of निर् + आ + √कृ, ‘thrust away, expelled’; the same word describes the gods driven from heaven by Mahiṣa (2.7).

mantras.anvaya: ताभ्याम् महासुराभ्याम् हृताधिकाराः निराकृताः (च) सर्वे त्रिदशाः ताम् अपराजिताम् देवीम् संस्मरन्ति।
mantras.anvaya_en: The participles हृताधिकाराः and निराकृताः (with the agent ताभ्याम् महासुराभ्याम्) describe the subject त्रिदशाः; the main verb is संस्मरन्ति with its object देवीम्.
mantras.lit: Deprived of their offices, all the Thirty, cast out by those two great asuras, call to mind that Goddess, the Unconquered.
mantras.tr: Robbed of their offices and driven out by the two great asuras, all the gods turned their minds to that Goddess, the Unconquered One.
mantras.tr_note: The historic present संस्मरन्ति is rendered as a past.

comm.t: The gods do not fight back; they remember. The verb सं-√स्मृ prepares the next verse, where the boon they recall was given precisely for remembrance. The Goddess is called Aparājitā, ‘unconquered’, in the verse after the gods were called पराजिताः, ‘conquered’.

The remembrance answers the end of the fourth chapter: there the gods asked that whenever she was remembered she would destroy their calamities (4.35–36), and she consented (4.39). The third story begins by invoking that promise.
